q-15707.solution:
First, let $u=@@D@@.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{@@N@@}{@@D@@}\,\text{d}x & =@@N@@\int \frac{1}{@@D@@}\,\text{d}x \\  & =@@N@@\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =@@N@@\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =@@N@@\operatorname{ln}⁡|@@D@@|+C\end{aligned}
$$
